💷 The latest ONS figures are out, and they matter for every household before the Budget.

📊 Borrowed in August: £18.3 BILLION
📈 £3.5bn more than the official forecast
📅 Second-highest August on record (behind 2020)
⚠️ Year so far: £8.1bn OVER plan

What's driving it? Welfare spending and debt interest. Debt interest alone was £8.8bn in August — the highest August since records began in 1997.

To be fair, borrowing so far this year is a bit lower than last year. But the Government is well off its OWN plan, five weeks before the Budget. 🤔

There are two ways to close a gap: spend less or tax more. I know which one I'd bet this government picks.
